draft.body:
For founders and operations leaders, swift, accurate reporting is crucial. Integrating AI offers speed, but only if it's anchored in verifiable facts.

My work on MedFlow Africa explores this by structuring AI to draft critical supply reports. This project helps review medicine stock-out risks and identify safe redistribution options.

The system uses AI to construct report narratives, but with a strict rule: it only selects and sequences pre-verified facts and approved phrasing. All specific numbers, names, and factual sentences are inserted by the system, ensuring the AI does not invent information or 'hallucinate'.

This approach delivers clear, accessible supply briefs for decision-makers, enhancing KPI reporting and business intelligence without compromising factual integrity. It means leaders get narrative support that clarifies complex data, making decisions faster and more reliable.

The real power of AI in decision support emerges when we constrain it with verified truth, focusing its capabilities on framing accurate data, not generating unchecked content.

This prototype uses synthetic inventory data to demonstrate the workflow. You can explore the application's interface.
Try the app: https://medflow-africa.vercel.app
Explore the repository: https://github.com/alumond/medflow-africa

By prioritizing factual summaries and controlled generation, we build business intelligence tools that genuinely support growth through reliable information.

draft.visual_prompt:
An authentic project screenshot of the MedFlow Africa application's 'District Overview' page. The screen displays key metrics, risk assessments for different facilities, and data quality indicators in a clean, professional user interface with clear headings and data tables. The design uses a muted color palette with emphasis on readability and hierarchical information presentation, showing a summary of medicine supply status across a district. The screenshot is sourced from MedFlow Africa's GitHub repository: docs/screenshots/01-district-overview.png.
Required visual direction: Preserve the highest native image quality. Capture app screens at 3x pixel density, normally 4800x3360 lossless PNG. Use imagegen at its highest available native quality. Never upscale small images or use lossy recompression. Check sharp edges and text at full size and readable key labels at phone size. Polished editorial graphics and clear data visuals with a strong complete title, generous spacing, short readable captions, and a concrete connection to the post. Codex-generated images must use relevant symbols, icons and diagrams to explain the idea. Give these visuals enough space to be understood at phone size. Keep text to a short title, labels and brief captions. Reject paragraphs in boxes and layouts where icons are only small decorations around text. For workflow posts, visualize the actual workflow discussed in the post: inputs, ordered steps, decisions, handoffs, relevant revision or failure paths, and outputs. Use a process map for sequential steps, a decision flow for branching logic, or swimlanes when ownership across people and tools matters. Show only steps and connections supported by the post and its evidence; label proposed workflows as proposed. Use real portfolio screenshots where relevant and label illustrative data explicitly. Every image must be visually inspected at phone size. Avoid: sketches and hand-drawn illustrations, model drawings and wireframes, generic AI artwork and decorative stick figures, internal drafting notes or placeholder text in artwork, truncated headlines and unlabeled decorative charts, dark 3D boardroom scenes by default, unlabeled abstract metaphors, unreadable tiny UI text, misspelled generated text, neon-by-default, glowing brains and circuit-board cliches, robot faces and generic AI imagery, sparse skeleton diagrams, text-only quote cards, paragraphs in boxes with only decorative icons, synthetic photorealism.
